summary: Marketing Pack (iter 26) — backend + frontend tests all pass. 12/12 backend pytest cases green, including admin gating, brand-aware PDFs, ZIP bundling, updated investor data-room.zip with 3 marketing PDFs, and FedEx brand swap. Frontend /marketing-pack page renders fully with admin cookie auth: hub, 3 download cards, ZIP button, tabs, 3 LinkedIn posts (incl. hashtag pills + copy), 3 cold-email templates (incl. merge tokens + follow-up + copy buttons + toast). Sidebar nav link present.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/marketing.py keeps all editorial copy hard-coded — fine for launch, but consider extracting to a JSON/YAML asset under /app/backend/data/marketing/ so non-engineers can edit posts without a deploy.

MarketingPack.jsx triggerDownload() reads session_token from localStorage but axios api lib uses withCredentials cookies — duplicated auth strategies; either align both on the cookie or persist token on login to both. Currently works because cookies are set by login flow, but the localStorage fallback may be stale.
pack.zip rebuilds PDFs synchronously inside the request (5 PDFs ~ 1.5 MB) — fine for admin-only endpoint but consider memoizing by brand_id if traffic grows.
Hashtag pills/CTA text use accent color on dark navy — contrast is acceptable but borderline for WCAG AA on the smallest font size (10-11px). Consider boosting weight or increasing alpha.
test_credentials: Admin Bearer test_session_admin_1 via Authorization header (backend) and `session_token` cookie + localStorage (frontend).
seed_data_creation: None — all marketing content is statically defined in routes/marketing.py.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter26 covers marketing pack. Use /app/backend/tests/test_iter26_marketing.py as regression. Brand-swap test transiently activates FedEx then restores orisei-freight; if a prior test leaves a non-Orisei brand active, run POST /api/branding/activate {brand_id:'orisei-freight'} first. Frontend tests need a session_token cookie set on the preview domain BEFORE navigating — localStorage alone is insufficient because api.js uses withCredentials cookie auth.
